subject: Making awkward kitchen spaces useful
hook: Standard kitchen units come in fixed widths. Ours start at whatever width the gap actually is.
ig:
Standard kitchen units come in fixed widths. Ours start at whatever width the gap actually is.

That's the whole reason awkward kitchen spaces can be made useful. When a unit is cut, edged and drilled to order, there's no need for a wide filler panel to cover a shortfall.

What you're seeing in our Hanley workshop:

- Board cut to the exact width on the sliding table panel saw.
- Visible edges sealed on the edge bander with ABS edging.
- Holes for runners and fixings drilled on the multi-spindle boring machine.
- The carcass assembled on the bench, so it arrives ready to fit.

No flat-pack, no self-assembly. Every unit is put together by us before it goes in the van, or on site where access means it has to be.

Got a gap in your kitchen that's never been used properly? DM us its rough width and what's either side, and we'll tell you what could go there.
fb:
This is what 'bespoke' actually looks like in our workshop.

When a kitchen has a gap that doesn't match standard sizes, we don't cover it with a panel. We cut a unit to that width, edge it, drill it and assemble it right here in Hanley, then our own team fits it.

That's how a narrow space beside the fridge becomes a pull-out for baking trays, or a tight corner becomes proper storage.

If you've got an awkward bit of kitchen that's been bugging you, have a look at our bespoke kitchen page:
https://superiofurniture.com/bespoke-kitchens/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=kitchen-planning-month&utm_content=day-226
